title: Beatrix and the Parish
premise: In the fog-bound parish of Wrenlow, coroner Silas Montrose is handed the cold case of Beatrix Hale, a young woman who vanished eleven years ago — until her diary surfaces in a donated book lot, its entries continuing for three years past her disappearance. As Silas follows the diary's coded references through parish records, gravestones, and half-buried family secrets, they realize the writer knows things only the dead should know, and that someone in Wrenlow has been quietly erasing evidence for a decade. The trail leads to the parish's beloved founding family, whose inheritance was secured by Beatrix's silence, and to a killer still living comfortably among the congregation. In the end, Silas stages a false exhumation to force the killer into the churchyard at night, closes the case Beatrix wrote herself, and finally gives her a grave with her name spoken aloud.
about_author: Orsen Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rural parish records before turning to fiction full-time. He writes mysteries obsessed with what paper remembers and people prefer to forget, and lives near the coast with an untidy garden and a dog named Ledger.

chapters.title: The Lot from the Estate Sale
chapters.summary: Silas Montrose, sorting a donated estate lot for the parish archive, finds a diary inscribed Beatrix Hale — a girl who vanished in 2013. The final entry is dated four years after she disappeared. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: unease dressed as professional curiosity; the first crack in Silas's belief that every case can be closed.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Silas walks the churchyard at dawn, confirming Beatrix has no marker, and interviews the rector, who insists the diary must be a hoax or a copycat. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet grief; the town's polite refusal to remember, establishing belonging as something Wrenlow grants selectively.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Reading the diary closely, Silas finds coded references — initials, dates, a recurring phrase about 'the blue door' — matching unsolved details never made public. Someone authentic continued writing after the disappearance. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dawning dread; the case file itself becomes untrustworthy.

chapters.title: The Montrose Method
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Silas learned record-keeping from their predecessor, old Coroner Vane, who once buried a mistake rather than report it. POV: Silas (past and present braided). Emotional beat: inheritance of guilt; Silas recognizes how institutions protect themselves, foreshadowing the parish's rot.

chapters.title: A Visitor Who Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: An anonymous note arrives quoting the diary verbatim — including a page Silas hasn't shown anyone. The writer warns them off. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: violation and thrill; the hunter realizes they are also being hunted.

chapters.title: The Founding Family
chapters.summary: Silas investigates the Ashcombe estate, whose matriarch endowed the church and whose son, Edmund, was the last person seen with Beatrix. The family's fortune traces to land transferred weeks after her disappearance. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling toward certainty; money and memory entwined.

chapters.title: Blue Door
chapters.summary: Following the diary's phrase, Silas locates a derelict cottage with a painted-blue cellar door and finds scratch marks, a child's shoe, and signs someone recently swept it clean. POV: alternating Silas and diary excerpts in Beatrix's voice. Emotional beat: horror arriving sideways; the past was here all along, maintained by careful hands.

chapters.title: What the Rector Knew
chapters.summary: Under pressure, the aging rector admits he was told to log Beatrix as a runaway and did so without question. His confession costs him his composure — and possibly his safety. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: complicity of good men; belonging purchased with silence.

chapters.title: Diary of a Ghost
chapters.summary: A full interlude chapter in Beatrix's voice: her last months alive, her fear of someone she calls only 'the Keeper,' her plan to hide the truth where only a reader would look. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: intimacy with the victim; she becomes a person, not a file.

chapters.title: The Keeper Identified
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing handwriting samples from parish ledgers, Silas narrows the Keeper to two candidates: Edmund Ashcombe or his late mother's secretary, Miriam Pell, who still keeps the estate keys. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: narrowing focus; every ally now looks like a suspect.

chapters.title: Miriam's Keys
chapters.summary: Silas confronts Miriam, who reveals she found Beatrix's body in 2016 and was paid by the Ashcombes to keep it secret — but swears she never touched the diary. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: pity tangled with fury; another life bent around the family's secret.

chapters.title: Exhumation Denied
chapters.summary: Silas petitions to open the unmarked plot behind the cottage; the magistrate, an Ashcombe cousin, refuses on procedural grounds. That night, Silas's office is searched. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: institutional walls closing in; the law itself is part of the inheritance.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: Miriam, frightened, produces a second notebook — the Keeper's own log of the cover-up, with dates, payments, and one chilling line: 'If the coroner asks, close the coroner.' POV: Silas. Emotional beat: escalation; the threat turns personal and imminent.

chapters.title: Vane's Mistake
chapters.summary: Digging into old Coroner Vane's sealed files, Silas discovers he falsified Beatrix's initial missing-person timeline — bought off in 2013, dead by 2017 under vague circumstances. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief and resolve; Silas sees their own possible ending in Vane's fate.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Silas stakes out the blue-door cottage and catches a figure burning papers inside — Edmund Ashcombe, who flees when confronted, leaving behind a charred corner bearing Beatrix's handwriting. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: adrenaline and doubt; proof, but not enough of it.

chapters.title: Confession Interrupted
chapters.summary: Edmund, cornered at the estate, begins to confess — then collapses from poisoning. Someone silenced him first. Silas realizes the true Keeper is still active and closer than assumed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: whiplash; the suspect becomes the second victim.

chapters.title: The Hand in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Forensic comparison finally matches the diary's later entries to the rector's own hand — he has been writing as Beatrix for years, a penance that became a prison, while the original murder belongs to someone else entirely. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: vertigo; the central mystery inverts.

chapters.title: Where She Was Buried
chapters.summary: The dying rector whispers the location: beneath the church floor, under the slab of the Ashcombe pew, placed there so the family would sit above her forever. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the crime was a message of ownership all along.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Churchyard
chapters.summary: Silas announces a public exhumation of the church floor, forcing the killer — the magistrate, protecting the inheritance and his own role in the 2013 cover-up — to come destroy the evidence by night. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: controlled tension; the trap set with the killer's own knowledge of the file.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Parish
chapters.summary: Confrontation among the graves: the magistrate confesses as Silas springs the trap, witnesses hidden among the headstones, police arriving on cue. He killed Beatrix when she threatened to expose the forged land transfer. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax; justice executed with precision and no small personal cost.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Beatrix is properly exhumed, identified, and buried under a stone bearing her name; the town attends in uncomfortable numbers. Silas reads her final diary entry at the service. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: mourning and release; memory restored to the community that erased it.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Silas donates both diaries to the archive, uncatalogued no longer, and writes the closing report in their own hand — the first entry in a new ledger titled Cases Worth Keeping. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; belonging earned by refusing to forget.
